title: The Ross Russell book and Charlie Parker
summary: He denies the book's story of an argument with Parker over a Coast date.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Bird reminds me of something--someone asked me, you're going to go up and talk to George, ask him about how he and Bird got into a hassle, that he wouldn't play with Bird or Bird wouldn't play with him, whatever, on a date; I don't know. Do you remember that, am I making that up?

You're repeating something that somebody showed me in a book that was written by Ross Russell, in which Ross Russell was talking about a jazz date that we were doing out on the coast, Bird and Diz and I think Lucky Thompson was on it, Arvin Garrison, myself; it was a bunch of people that Ross Russell had gathered together and on the night of the date two of the guys were busted in California, in town and didn't arrive at the date. There was a big thing about postponing it and changing men and how it came out to an argument between Bird and me about who wouldn't play with who, I read about in Ross' book. It never happened; I never had an argument with him in my life, other than about shit when he refused to give me some when we were both strung out; that was all, one argument.
Is it fair to ask you, who is the favorite jazz player you ever played with? And define it any way you want.
I'll tell you this, if Bird had said in those days I don't want to
play with him because he's not up to our caliber, I would have agreed with him. I would have said he's telling the truth, but we never had a situation as described in that book.
Man, I hear stories about me during the years that would make great books, but fictional books.
